A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same BabyVision research work and are fully readable, including Appendices A–C. Pages 2–26 have identical extracted text and rendered content; differences are confined to the title page.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, child and adult human studies, generation experiments, judge validation, and RLVR fine-tuning results in Sections 5–6 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, human evaluations, judge validation, and RLVR experiments.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, generative task formulation, automatic judging procedures, and GRPO fine-tuning procedure are identical in both versions.

E1.justification: Both retain BabyVision's 388 questions across 22 subtypes, BabyVision-Gen's 280 questions across 21 subtypes, BabyVision-Mini, and the 1,400 training examples. Task coverage and human populations are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1–3 and 6, including proprietary and open MLLMs, image generators, and Qwen3VL variants. Human comparisons and the video-generation examples in Figure 9 are also retained.

E3.justification: Inference settings, evaluation prompts and judges, metrics, training budgets, and human-study sample sizes and procedures are unchanged in Sections 3–6 and Appendices A–B.

E4.justification: Both contain the same scaling and thinking-mode comparisons, RLVR analyses, failure cases, generation examples, and automatic-judge validation. No ablation or supplementary analysis is added, removed, or revised.

E5.justification: Tables 1–3 and 6 retain the same three-run averages and standard deviations. Error bars and other statistical reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are retained. For example, Table 1 still reports Gemini3-Pro-Preview at 49.7% and humans at 94.1%; Table 3 retains NanoBanana-Pro at 18.3%; Table 7 retains the GRPO comparison of 13.1% versus 17.9%.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs. Task definitions and evaluation criteria are identical, with no added or revised mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about foundational visual deficits, the human–model gap, BabyVision, and BabyVision-Gen with its evaluation toolkit.

C2.justification: The verbalization-bottleneck explanation, four failure modes, interpretation of RLVR effects, and limitations of visual generation are unchanged. The single-school population caveat and warning against directly comparing the two benchmarks are also retained.

D1.justification: Implementation details, appendix prompts, and code/data access information are identical. Section 6.2 retains the same GRPO hyperparameters, eight H800 GPUs, approximately three days of training, and 18 epochs.

R1.justification: Section 2, research-positioning passages, and the complete reference list are identical. No cited work or novelty relationship is added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 adds Ming Wu and the affiliation 0G Labs to the title page and updates the header date and arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose, terminology, section order, and appendices are unchanged.

P2.justification: The title-page author and affiliation lines are slightly reflowed to accommodate the addition. All figures, tables, captions, and the layout of pages 2–26 remain identical.

improvement.justification: v2 changes authorship information and dates, with minor title-page reflow. The scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and appendices are unchanged, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
